Events are delivered asynchronously to your app and you can only observe the event; you cannot modify or otherwise prevent the event from being delivered to its original target application. Key-related events may only be monitored if accessibility is enabled or if your application is trusted for accessibility access (see AXIsProcessTrusted in AXUIElement.h). Note that your handler will not be called for events that are sent to your own application.

543:    Use +addLocal to install an event monitor that receives events before they are dispatched by -[NSApplication sendEvent:]. In this case, your block should either return a valid NSEvent (which may be the same as the incoming NSEvent, or may be a newly created NSEvent) to cause the event to be dispatched, or it may return nil to stop dispatching of the event. Note that your handler will not be called for events that are consumed by nested event-tracking loops such as control tracking, menu tracking, or window dragging; only events that are dispatched through -[NSApplication sendEvent:] will be passed to your handler.

546:
